location.description: Kleinburg is a historic heritage village in the northwestern corner of the City of Vaughan, Ontario. Located approximately 30km northwest of downtown Toronto between branches of the Humber River. Heritage Conservation District under the Ontario Heritage Act. Bordered by Highway 400 to the east and Highway 27 to the west.
location.commute_notes: GO Bus service on main street. Vaughan Metropolitan Centre subway ~40 min drive connecting to Toronto subway. Village itself is car-dependent for most residents.

home_types.construction_notes: Mix of heritage homes in village core (pre-1960), 1980-2000 executive builds, and recent luxury estate construction post-2010

transit.go_bus: GO Bus stop on Islington Avenue (main street) — service to Hwy 400 corridor
transit.subway_nearest: Vaughan Metropolitan Centre (VMC) subway station — York-Spadina extension — ~40 min drive. Direct to downtown Toronto.
transit.walk_score_note: Village core walkable for shops/cafes. Surrounding estate areas fully car-dependent.

secondary_catholic.name: St. Jean de Brebeuf Catholic High School

parks_and_recreation.mcmichael_trail: 1.5km trail down into Humber River Valley connecting to Bindertwine Park

amenities.landmark: McMichael Canadian Art Collection — 100 acres, 7,000+ works, Group of Seven, First Nations art. Crown corporation of Ontario since 1972.
amenities.village_core: Islington Avenue — boutique shops, cafes (Cookie Crumble Café), restaurants (Avenue Cibi e Vini, The Doctor's House), spas, galleries
amenities.nearby_big_box: Vaughan Mills Mall (~15 min), Woodbridge retail corridors

history.founded: 1848 by German settler John Nicholas Kline (Henry Klein served as first postmaster and Reeve of Vaughan Township 1859-1860)
history.heritage_status: Heritage Conservation District under Ontario Heritage Act — protects village character
history.mcmichael_gallery_history: Robert and Signe McMichael purchased land in 1951. First acquisition: Tom Thomson painting for C$250 in 1955. Donated to Province of Ontario in 1965 (194 works, buildings, land). Formally incorporated as Crown corporation November 1972.
history.mills: Original economy based on flour and wheat mills along Humber River
history.group_of_seven_connection: McMichaels and six members of the Group of Seven are buried in the McMichael cemetery on the gallery grounds
